entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on attention that was owed and not paid, so it carries a sense of duty unmet that *ignored* does not.
examples: Shaw's neglected one-act comedy, ‘A Village Wooing’

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of the three: it grants that something stood there to be attended to, without *ignored*'s deliberateness or *neglected*'s failure of care.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A miss rather than a refusal - it concedes that the thing should have entered the reckoning and quietly admits the error.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat where *overlooked* is apologetic: it says only that nothing was made of the thing, conceding no mistake.
examples: his retirement was not allowed to go unmarked

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The barest of the three - the plain negative of taking something into account, with no suggestion that anyone should have.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the shadow of someone who might have noticed, so it can be a relief as easily as a slight.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatly sensory beside *unobserved* - nothing registered, with no watcher implied for the thing to have escaped.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and abstract, covering both the failure to register a thing and the silence that follows, with its weight on the registering.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Holds the same pair tipped the other way - the thing may well have been seen, and the point is that nothing was said of it.

entries.definition: not original; not being or productive of something fresh and unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat statement of the fault - nothing fresh in the thing and nothing fresh coming out of it - delivered without the scorn *trite* carries.
examples: his life had been unoriginal, conforming completely to the given pattern

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissal rather than description: the repetition has emptied the thing out, where *commonplace* only notes that it has been met before.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest reproach in the set - it registers the overfamiliarity and stops there, leaving the contempt to *banal*.
examples: his remarks were trite and commonplace

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A formal-sounding verdict that the thing has been run into the ground, heavier and more deliberate than *tired*.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and offhand: it shrugs at how familiar the thing has become instead of condemning it the way *banal* does.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The overuse leaves a mark, as though the thing had been handled until the shine came off it - grubbier than *well-worn*.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest word here - it files the endless repetition almost as a category rather than a fault, with none of the disgust in *trite*.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The wear has gone all the way through: the thing still holds its shape but has nothing left in it, harsher than *well-worn*.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Softer than the rest, because it lays the wearing at time's door rather than anyone's, so the reproach lands gently.
